look_here_first: Think small granite spiderwort: a short narrow-leaved perennial on Llano-Uplift granitic soils, with unusually long flower pedicels and sparse glandular hairs on stems, pedicels, and sepals.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small clump-forming perennial usually 10–40 cm tall

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaf surfaces nearly glabrous to sparsely hairy

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: pedicels and sepals sparsely to moderately glandular-pubescent

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: fascicle of distally thickened tuberous roots

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: strong association with granite, gneiss, and derived sandy-gravelly soils

lookalikes.differences: Habitat plus stature is powerful: T. pedicellata is the small narrow-leaved granite specialist; T. edwardsiana is taller and broad-leaved; T. hirsutiflora has slender fibrous roots and favors sandy eastern-Texas habitats.
